rv.q: Classic Stage Company's triumphant Off-Broadway revival of the underrated 2002 chamber musical 'A Man of No Importance,' starring Jim Parsons and directed by John Doyle, comes as a most welcome and most unexpected surprise.

Parsons convincingly inhabits Alfie's earnestness and diffidence, if not his Irish accent. Alfie's intimate little story of self-discovery isn't quite big enough for all its characters, but each member of the ensemble shines in even the most underwritten parts.
Doyle's production remains oddly lifeless — and even moments of violence pass by without so much as a blip to raise the blood pressure.

Mr. Parsons seems not to understand the pathos of his character, choosing instead to mope across the stage in an aimless search for Alfie, the character who chooses less to be pitied and more to be understood and accepted unconditionally.
